title: Reading Theory and Interpretation
text:
Literary criticism has long been divided over whether a text should be read as a window onto its author's intentions or as a self-sufficient structure of meaning. Formalists insisted that the poem itself, rather than the biography of the poet, was the proper object of analysis. Later theorists, however, argued that every reading is shaped by the assumptions of the reader, and that meaning is never simply deposited in a text. Such debates are not merely academic; they determine what counts as a legitimate interpretation.

Deconstruction, associated with Jacques Derrida, pushed this skepticism further by showing how texts undermine their own apparent certainties. A close reading, in this view, reveals tensions that the author may not have consciously intended. Critics who follow this method rarely offer a definitive verdict; instead, they expose the instability of the language. Many students find this approach frustrating, yet it has permanently altered how literature is taught.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what did the Formalists insist should be the object of analysis?
According to the second paragraph, what does a close reading of deconstruction reveal?
options: Tensions the author may not have intended

questions.text: Why might a deconstructive critic avoid giving a definitive verdict on a text?
options: They have not finished reading the text
They believe the language of a text is unstable and resists final judgment
They think the author's intentions are irrelevant to every reader
University rules require them to stay neutral

questions.text: What can be inferred about the effect of these critical debates?
options: They have little practical effect on how literature is studied
They shape which interpretations are considered acceptable
They were fully resolved by the Formalists
They concern only the biographies of poets

vocabulary.definition: fully accepted as valid, reasonable or allowed
doubt about whether claims or beliefs are true
final and not open to further dispute
the quality of being changeable or not firmly fixed

paragraph_translations: La crítica literaria ha estado dividida durante mucho tiempo sobre si un texto debe leerse como una ventana a las intenciones de su autor o como una estructura de significado autosuficiente. Los formalistas insistían en que el poema en sí, y no la biografía del poeta, era el objeto apropiado de análisis. Sin embargo, teóricos posteriores sostuvieron que toda lectura está moldeada por los supuestos del lector, y que el significado nunca se deposita simplemente en un texto. Estos debates no son meramente académicos; determinan qué se considera una interpretación legítima.

La deconstrucción, asociada con Jacques Derrida, llevó este escepticismo más lejos al mostrar cómo los textos socavan sus propias certezas aparentes. Una lectura atenta, desde esta perspectiva, revela tensiones que el autor quizás no pretendió conscientemente. Los críticos que siguen este método rara vez ofrecen un veredicto definitivo; en cambio, exponen la inestabilidad del lenguaje. Muchos estudiantes encuentran frustrante este enfoque, pero ha cambiado de forma permanente la manera en que se enseña la literatura.
